newsitem.title: CHINA: China to air TV tribute to paramount leader Deng.
newsitem.headline: China to air TV tribute to paramount leader Deng.

text.p: China will launch primetime broadcasts of a 12-part documentary praising ailing paramount leader Deng Xiaoping on January 1, 1997, television officials said on Thursday.

The documentary, to be aired daily by the state-run China Central Television (CCTV) station, would focus on the achievements of the 92-year-old political patriarch, said an official of the military section of CCTV's programming department.
"This is a record of a great man," said the official, who declined to be identified.

A senior Beijing official said on Monday that Deng, who is believed to be suffering from Parkinson's Disease, was in good health, but could be unable to realise his long-cherished wish to visit Hong Kong for the ceremony of its return to Chinese rule next year.
The television official said CCTV's timing of the broadcasts had not been influenced by concerns about Deng's health.
He dismissed suggestions the programmes were aimed at deifying the mastermind of China's switch from strict communist central planning to a booming market-style economy, saying Deng was no god.
"He is an ordinary great elderly man," the official said.
The Deng documentary had taken four years to complete and included interviews with more than 100 senior officials, the official Xinhua news agency said.
Much of the content of the documentary was being made public for the first time, the agency said but gave no details.

Deng's health and the political succession that will follow it has long been the subject of intense speculation in China and elsewhere, although analysts say that his death has now largely been discounted.

On Monday, Beijing Vice-Mayor Zhang Baifa, who is believed to be close to the Deng family, said that while Deng had vowed to visit Hong Kong during the British colony's return to Chinese rule on June 30, 1997, that could be impossible.

"It would be difficult for him to go now. It would be disastrous for an old man in his 90s to catch cold. Catching cold would be a serious illness," said Zhang, adding that as far as he knew Deng was in good health.
